items.title: Marilyn Crispell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 21, 2022
items.q: I wondered like did the musicians accompanying her ever feel like okay, we should slow down. No. Well no. I wouldn’t think so because I would think they were keeping the thing, they were keeping the structure happening which allowed her to be very flexible.

ctx.x: Um hum. Yeah. I think there’s a lot of truth in that. Going with somebody also has to has different connotations to me. Like okay you could try to join them in the harmonies that they’re playing, or you could try to play— not go with them in that way but do something that would be different but still work with what they’re doing. You know? And in fact sometimes when I was improvising ballads with the trio I would just start playing something, changing harmonies and all that. And I would tell people, “Don’t try to…

Yeah you gave me a flash of listening to some Billie Holiday records where she was so far — not so far, but she was really quite behind the beat. I wondered like did the musicians accompanying her ever feel like okay, we should slow down.
No. Well no. I wouldn’t think so because I would think they were keeping the thing, they were keeping the structure happening which allowed her to be very flexible.
